# Kredoxi durable architectural truth

## Project purpose
Kredoxi reduces credential exposure in declarative configuration through
authenticated, policy-controlled runtime resolution. It is conventional
software, not an AI agent. References are not secrets.

## Architecture and operating model
Go standard-library-only explicit resolver over loopback mutual TLS 1.3.
`cmd/broker`, `cmd/consumer`, and `cmd/synthetic-service` are independently
executable Go commands. `cmd/demo` launches them as separate processes over
loopback TLS 1.3 and sends synthetic bootstrap material through bounded stdin
pipes without writing private keys or credentials to files. The supervisor
also holds the synthetic fixture and serialized bootstrap payloads in memory
for demo/redaction checks. It builds binaries in a temporary directory,
captures output, and waits for child exit before cleanup. Linux direct children
use a parent-death signal and separate process group; Windows uses a
kill-on-close Job Object. Other operating systems have no added containment
guarantee. This demonstrates process separation, not OS-account enforcement,
executable identity, arbitrary descendant cleanup, same-user protection or
transparent interception.

`internal/resolver` owns grammar, immutable policy, client, broker and telemetry.
`internal/synthetic` owns an ephemeral development CA. `examples` contains only
non-secret references and policy; private keys and generated credentials are
not read from or persisted to files.

## Durable constraints and trust boundaries
All bundled core invariants remain unchanged. Additional product controls live
in [Kredoxi controls](kredoxi-controls.md), the active PR contract and
[security documentation](../../../docs/security.md).
The client trusts a dedicated ephemeral CA and IP SAN, not system roots.
The broker trusts a verified client certificate URI SAN and then checks exact
reference policy. Key possession does not attest executable identity.
OS-native IPC and OS identity enforcement are undecided; an Architecture ADR
and owner approval are required before selecting or claiming either.
Provider values are ordinary Go memory; an authorized application can extract
them. Same-user/privileged key theft, process compromise and memory dumps remain
outside demonstrated protection.

## Governance
cARL v1.0.2, upstream source `goldjg/cARL` tag v1.0.2. The Go MVP profile retains
every core pack plus Go, PowerShell tooling and CI. Other conditional packs
remain installed/selected, not active. Managed baseline controls and adapters
remain canonical; product-specific controls are additive and user-owned.
The inherited upstream memory is retained only as
`upstream-memory-reference.md`; its cARL-product roadmap is not Kredoxi truth.

## Commands and evidence
Require Go 1.27.3 or newer patched supported toolchain. Initial Go 1.27.0
vulnerability scan identified standard-library advisories; 1.27.3 cleared the
same symbol-level scan. `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go run ./cmd/demo`.
Race testing requires cgo and a C compiler; mandatory Linux CI covers it.
Security evidence and caveats are in `docs/security.md`; never equate tests or
governance diagnostics with complete prevention guarantees.

## Open questions
License selection, production enrollment, OS-peer-authenticated IPC,
signed policy/antirollback, provider lifecycle and protected telemetry sinks.
